```{r setup, eval = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
rm(list = ls())

source("constants.R")
source("loadToMySqlConfiguration.R")

install_if_missing("RMySQL")
```

```{r connectMySQL, eval = TRUE, warning = FALSE, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
mysql_con <- dbConnect(
  RMySQL::MySQL(),
  host     = etl.mysql.host,
  port     = etl.mysql.port,
  user     = etl.mysql.user,
  password = etl.mysql.password,
  dbname   = etl.mysql.dbname
)
cat("Connected to MySQL.\n")
```

# 1. Data Warehouse Overview

Below is the expense analysis datamart that has been created for Heracletes Advisors PC. The datamart is constructed using a star schema design where the `expense_facts` fact table is connected to the following dimension tables: date, employee, client, project, category, currency, and merchant.

**Sign Clarification:** The amounts are based on the source system's convention that any negative number is an expense charged to the card, while any positive number is an amount credited/refunded.

```{sql overviewCounts, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM expense_facts) AS total_facts,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dim_employee)  AS total_employees,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dim_client)    AS total_clients,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dim_project)   AS total_projects,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dim_category)  AS total_categories
```

# 2. Total and Average Expense per Category per Quarter

This query tests the slicing capability of the fact table across expense categories aggregated by quarter. It demonstrates the core analytical requirement: expense totals and averages per category per time period.

```{sql expenseByCategory, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT dc.category_name,
       ef.year,
       ef.quarter,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       ROUND(AVG(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS avg_expense,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_category dc ON ef.category_key = dc.category_key
 GROUP BY dc.category_name, ef.year, ef.quarter
 ORDER BY ef.year, ef.quarter, total_expense
 LIMIT 20
```

# 3. Total Expenses per Client per Project per Month

This query exercises the primary analytical slice required by the requirements: expense totals and averages broken down by client, project, and month. Since client and project assignments were not present in the SQLite source schema, transactions are grouped under the stub 'Unassigned' entries.

```{sql expenseByClientProject, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT dcl.client_name,
       dp.project_name,
       ef.year,
       ef.month,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       ROUND(AVG(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS avg_expense,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_client  dcl ON ef.client_key  = dcl.client_key
  JOIN dim_project dp  ON ef.project_key = dp.project_key
 GROUP BY dcl.client_name, dp.project_name, ef.year, ef.month
 ORDER BY dcl.client_name, dp.project_name, ef.year, ef.month
 LIMIT 20
```

# 4. Monthly Expense Trend

This query shows total and average expenses by month across all years, joined to the date dimension to retrieve the month name. It is useful for identifying seasonal spending patterns.

```{sql monthlyTrend, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT ef.year,
       ef.month,
       dd.month_name,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       ROUND(AVG(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS avg_expense,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_date dd ON ef.date_key = dd.date_key
 GROUP BY ef.year, ef.month, dd.month_name
 ORDER BY ef.year, ef.month
```

# 5. Billable vs Non-Billable Expenses by Client

This query compares billable and non-billable expense totals per client, which is important for determining how much of each client's expenses can be recovered through billing.

```{sql billableAnalysis, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT dcl.client_name,
       CASE WHEN ef.billable = 1 THEN 'Billable' ELSE 'Non-Billable' END AS expense_type,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_client dcl ON ef.client_key = dcl.client_key
 GROUP BY dcl.client_name, ef.billable
 ORDER BY dcl.client_name, ef.billable DESC
```

# 6. Top 10 Expense Categories by Total Amount

This query surfaces the ten highest-spending category and subcategory combinations, ordered by total expense descending so the largest spends appear first.

```{sql topCategories, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT dc.category_name,
       dc.subcategory_name,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions,
       ROUND(AVG(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS avg_per_txn
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_category dc ON ef.category_key = dc.category_key
 GROUP BY dc.category_name, dc.subcategory_name
 ORDER BY total_expense DESC
 LIMIT 10
```

# 7. Expense per Employee per Quarter

This query shows total expenses per employee broken down by quarter, useful for identifying high-spending employees and monitoring travel budgets.

```{sql employeeExpenses, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT CONCAT(de.first_name, ' ', de.last_name) AS employee_name,
       ef.year,
       ef.quarter,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_employee de ON ef.employee_key = de.employee_key
 GROUP BY de.employee_key, de.first_name, de.last_name, ef.year, ef.quarter
 ORDER BY de.last_name, ef.year, ef.quarter
 LIMIT 20
```

# 8. Currency Distribution

This query shows how transactions are distributed across currencies, along with raw amount totals. This is relevant for Heracletes given its international client base where expenses occur in USD, BRL, Euro, and GBP.

```{sql currencyDistribution, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT dcu.currency_code,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.txn_amount), 2) AS total_raw_amount,
       ROUND(AVG(ef.txn_amount), 2) AS avg_raw_amount
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_currency dcu ON ef.currency_key = dcu.currency_key
 GROUP BY dcu.currency_code
 ORDER BY num_transactions DESC
```

# 9. Quarterly Expense by Client (Year-over-Year)

This query provides a year-over-year view of quarterly expenses per client, which is useful for tracking client billing trends over time.

```{sql quarterlyByClient, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT dcl.client_name,
       ef.year,
       ef.quarter,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       ROUND(AVG(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS avg_expense
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_client dcl ON ef.client_key = dcl.client_key
 GROUP BY dcl.client_name, ef.year, ef.quarter
 ORDER BY dcl.client_name, ef.year, ef.quarter
```

# 10. Full Analytical Slice: Category per Client per Project per Month per Quarter per Year

This is the primary fact table query the datamart was designed to support. It combines all the required dimensions in a single slice — category (rolled up from subcategory), client, project, month, quarter, and year — exactly as specified in the requirements.

```{sql fullSlice, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT dc.category_name,
       dcl.client_name,
       dp.project_name,
       ef.year,
       ef.quarter,
       ef.month,
       ROUND(SUM(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS total_expense,
       ROUND(AVG(ef.allocated_amount), 2) AS avg_expense,
       COUNT(*) AS num_transactions
  FROM expense_facts ef
  JOIN dim_category dc  ON ef.category_key = dc.category_key
  JOIN dim_client   dcl ON ef.client_key   = dcl.client_key
  JOIN dim_project  dp  ON ef.project_key  = dp.project_key
 GROUP BY dc.category_name, dcl.client_name, dp.project_name, ef.year, ef.quarter, ef.month
 ORDER BY ef.year, ef.quarter, ef.month, dcl.client_name, dp.project_name
 LIMIT 20
```

# 11. Partition and Index Verification

These queries confirm that the `expense_facts` table is correctly partitioned by year and that all indexes are in place, which is required by the practicum specification for fast analytical queries.

```{sql showPartitions, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SELECT PARTITION_NAME, TABLE_ROWS
  FROM information_schema.PARTITIONS
 WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'expense_facts'
   AND TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()
```

```{sql showIndexes, connection = mysql_con, author = "Siddhi Satish Bhanushali"}
SHOW INDEX FROM expense_facts
```
